chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: Chu Berry's fatal auto accident and the bus fire
summary: Cab's band came upon the wreck; Chu died, and the bus caught fire that night.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Where were you that night he had that auto accident?
We did a one-nighter that night. We were on our way to Toronto if I'm not mistaken. I forget where we played. Do you have it there?
Let's have a look just quickly. Let's see. After playing a one nighter with Cab in Brookfield, Ohio, Chu, Andy Brown and Lamar Wright set out by car for the
(2And near Conneaut, Ohio,)) right up on Lake Erie,
(the car skidded off the road and hit a concrete bridge.))
(Brown and Wright were only slightly hurt,
but Chu received severe head injuries and he died four days later without regaining consciousness.))

CC: That's right, and what happened that night, well they were in the car with Lamar Wright, Vernon Brown and Chu, and of course all of us were at the bus and we had to wait until the band boy loaded the bus, so we were half hour behind. So Cab, that Christmas Cab would always buy the band a nice jacket or give us a watch or something like that. Well he bought us all green jackets for Christmas, they were just beautiful. So the majority of the guys in the band had their jackets on that night. So anyway, after the bus got loaded, everybody got on the bus and we were riding on down the freeway, highway, and we saw these markers on the highway, you know where there was an accident ahead of us which was oh a few hundred feet way up, you know, and so they had this big light on the Greyhound buses, you know, and so we sit there for a while and never paid it any mind, just figured it was another accident until we'd been sitting there for quite a while and the driver just took that light and flashed it way up, you know which it
projected way up, we happened to see this green jacket....

So we all got out of the bus and trotted up there, and Chu was there lying, Lamar was crying, Brown he was there looking sad. Chu was hurting where his belt had broke and boy, then we lifted him back in the bus and called an ambulance and a couple days after that he died, you know, it was a terrible night. So anyway, that night that Chu passed we noticed Cab came on the bandstand. He was very sad that night, we probably figured something had happened, we hadn't received any word from the hospital as yet. Then after the dance is when Cab told us that Chu had passed. Then everybody was really brought down then. And on our way that same night, to another one nighter, the back end of our bus caught on fire, and my tom-toms were burnt halfway through. We were going through a little town and people were hollering at us but we thought that they were just waving at us because Cab had these banners on the bus, 'Cab Calloway and Orchestra' we thought that they were just hollering at us. They were telling us that the back end of the bus was burning. And everybody then said oh the hell with the road and everything, let's quit, we aren't going on the road any more. Well you know how those things are. It's a feeling that you get, you know, after going through a thing like Chu dying and then getting on the bus, and that was a very sad evening.
Very sad. Chu Berry. Great man. Great tenor
